items.title: Chuck Mancuso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 10, 2013
items.q: But we talked to McCoy. I was going you know, “Is that an e minor vamp” you know because Paul had shown me how to do a little bit of the “My Favorite Things” which I would play over and over, not well at all. And then Jimmy was nice to talk to. Elvin was just sort of aloof. But in between every set,

ctx.x: No I was so respectful. I’d stay out of the way. Because he was the show. I was just a sidekick. They didn’t know who I was and they didn’t really care. They figured I probably was his son. So I was an adjunct to him. He was the one. When we went into some of the white churches the same kind of thing happened. And so I learned all this stuff because of Bill. And he’d give me his notes, he’d show me how to do it and I’d go © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

visit him all the time. I remember him telling me one time Coltrane was in town and I called him up and I says, “McCoy Tyner just took a twenty-one minute solo.” I used to time everything you know. And he goes, “I can’t do it right now, Chuck, because I’m teaching country and folk and my whole head is in country and folk.” I didn’t understand it at the time. But he did his intro courses, which were the big draws, like my jazz-rock, now American popular music is a big draw. And then he did this special course,…
